extracted.intended_audience: CDC grant applicants, CDC program staff, and potential merit reviewers
extracted.subtask_short: CDC merit review process for grants
extracted.subtask_description: Describes CDC's standards and procedures for conducting merit review of grant applications, including reviewer eligibility, conflict-of-interest rules, scoring against NOFO criteria, confidentiality, and documentation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit review — independence and objectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Merit review is a process that involves the thorough and consistent examination of applications based on an unbiased evaluation of scientific or technical merit or other relevant aspects of the applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merit reviews ensure applications are evaluated through a process that is fair, equitable, objective, and transparent. All responsive applications for CDC grant funding are subject to merit review (whether in response to a NOFO, solicited single-source, or requesting post-award changes). The results of merit reviews are advisory and inform the approving program official's award recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsiveness / eligibility for merit review
rubrics_metrics.description: A responsive application is one that meets objective eligibility criteria outlined in the notice of funding opportunity and is accepted for merit review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only applications that meet the NOFO's objective eligibility criteria will be accepted for merit review; all such responsive applications are subject to the CDC merit review process regardless of solicitation type or post-award change requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory nature of merit review results
rubrics_metrics.description: The results of merit reviews are advisory in nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The approving program official is to consider the results when making final award recommendations. The approving program official has delegated authority to make funding decisions for a given program but cannot serve as the appointing official for reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviews conducted promptly after submission deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews are conducted as soon as possible after the application submission deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely scheduling of review activities is a standard CDC expectation to ensure prompt evaluation following the submission deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted review formats and approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Merit reviews for discretionary grant programs may be carried out through a variety of approaches such as face-to-face meetings, utilizing technology for remote discussions, or through independent assessment of individual reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CDC uses in-person, virtual, or independent written-review formats as appropriate. For reviews subject to the Federal Advisory Committee Act (FACA), CDC publishes specific times and places of committee meetings in the Federal Register and whether the meeting is open or closed to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation against NOFO-published criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are reviewed in accordance with evaluation criteria published in the NOFO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers score applications against the evaluation criteria published in the NOFO. The NOFO’s evaluation criteria are the authoritative basis for scoring and the preparation of summary statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only appointed reviewers may score applications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring is restricted to those reviewers officially appointed for the review. This preserves integrity of scoring and ensures only authorized reviewers' assessments are used in advisory recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of summary statements
rubrics_metrics.description: A summary statement of each application's strengths and weaknesses by criteria is prepared for each scored application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each scored application reviewers' assessments are synthesized into a summary statement organized by the published criteria, documenting strengths and weaknesses to inform program officials and applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of merit review documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Merit review documentation is handled in a way that protects confidentiality of the reviewers' identities, comments, and assessments or scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review records and reviewer-identifying information are managed to prevent disclosure of reviewer identities, comments, or scores, consistent with applicable policies and any FACA/open-meeting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer independence requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers for discretionary programs must be independent of the applicant or application they review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any individual with a function or position that may have a specific interest in the outcome of the review of a particular application is not eligible to be a reviewer for that application. Independence is required to maintain fairness and objectivity in discretionary program reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of ineligible reviewers (organizational conflicts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ineligible individuals include representatives from the CDC awarding program office, representatives from the servicing grants management office, any federal employee with a real or apparent conflict of interest, any consultant with a real or apparent COI, and individuals that have a direct relationship with the applicant organization or have a COI in the award of a grant to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CDC excludes individuals whose organizational role or relationships could create real or apparent conflicts (e.g., CDC program office staff, grants management staff) from serving as reviewers for affected applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of reviewer conflict of interest (COI) — personal and familial relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: A reviewer for discretionary programs has a COI in an application if that person or his or her spouse, parent, minor child, or partner: serves as an officer to the applicant, subsidiary, or parent organization; is negotiating prospective employment with the applicant, subsidiary, or parent organization; has a financial interest in the application; is a consultant on any application submitted under the NOFO; or has a known close friendship or relationship with key applicant staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CDC attempts to avoid circumstances that might introduce COI or the appearance of COI, or any prejudices, biases, or predispositions on the part of reviewers. This list operationalizes the types of personal, familial, financial, employment, and close-relationship situations that constitute conflicts for reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation of absence of COI by reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: CDC merit reviewers must complete a statement attesting to the absence of COI before reviewing any application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior to participation in a review, reviewers are required to affirm they have no real or apparent conflicts for the applications they will evaluate; this attestation supports enforcement of eligibility and COI standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretionary grant program definition and use of discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: A discretionary grant program is a grant program where, although the authorizing statute may define eligibility and certain parameters, an awarding agency is not required to make awards to all eligible entities and therefore has discretion, based on the outcome of an objective review process and application of other published factors, as to who receives an award and the amount of the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition explains the statutory and procedural context for discretionary programs and the role of merit review and other published factors in allocating awards.
